title: selliguea whitfordii
intro: Selliguea whitfordii, commonly known as the "wild ginseng" or "pahaydig," is a species of fern native to the Philippines. It has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, as well as its ability to improve digestion and boost the immune system. The therapeutic actions of Selliguea whitfordii include its potential to lower blood sugar levels, reduce blood pressure, and exhibit antimicrobial and antifungal properties. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include phenolic acids, flavonoids, and saponins, which have been identified in various studies on the plant's extracts.
